originality.rationale: The claim is the sharp ordinary and logarithmic densities in the word-length parameter of every nontrivial positive-order Rényi-entropy-deficit level set for the Fibonacci Sturmian measure. The exact finite-word frequency table is classical and is explicitly not claimed as new. The inspected three-distance theorem supplies the gap multiplicities but does not state either length density; the new statements require uniform Fibonacci-scale entropy profiles, proof of precisely two threshold crossings, summation across all scales and a separate logarithmic harmonic limit. A full text of the closest indexed finite-type-cover entropy claim was compared, and its mathematical object is different. No equal or dominating evaluated level-set density theorem was identified; earlier unindexed derivations remain possible.

value.rationale: A canonical Rényi/Shannon statistic for minimal-complexity uniquely ergodic dynamics has a natural unaddressed arithmetic question: which block lengths exhibit strongly nonuniform word frequencies? The answer gives sharp distinct liminf/limsup density, the entire accumulation interval, and an exact logarithmic density at every interior threshold and order q>0. The novel content is cross-scale threshold counting, not re-computing already-known word frequencies; it distinguishes ordinary from logarithmic information sampling and provides an exact structural benchmark.
